Shekhar Singh, Adv.
For the State : Mr. Fahad Allam, Addl.
P.P. Order No.04/Dated- 12.06.2024

Heard learned counsel
for the parties.

2.  The petitioner has been made accused in connection with Rajmahal P.S. Case No. 75 of 2023 registered under sections 302/34 of Indian Penal Code and after completion of investigation,
charge-sheet has been submitted for the offence under Section 306 IPC read with Section 34 IPC.
3.

Factual matrix of the case in a nutshell is that one Reena Karmakar lodged a written report on 16.03.2023 at Rajmahal Police Station District Sahibganj stating inter alia that on 15.03.2023 at about 04:00 p.m. while her husband had gone to Rajmahal court and she along with her son Deepak Karmakar were sitting at furniture shop at a distance of their house and her daughter Reena Kumari aged about 20 years was alone in the house.

It is alleged that in the meantime under a preplanned way and hatching conspiracy Arjun Mandal along with his family members namely Nemani Mandal,
Ram Krishan Mandal, Pintu Mandal, Shiv Kumar Karmakar, Ram Kumar Karmakar and Rupa Devi have approached to the house of the informant with evil motive to take revenge entered into the house and forcibly wrapped the neck of the informant daughter with Dupatta and hanged her to ceiling fan causing her death instantaneously in presence of informant and other persons.
The informant and her son protested against the above incident but alone then dead body of the deceased was brought to Sub-Divisional Hospital, Rajmahal where her daughter was declared dead.

4. It is further alleged that there was love affair since two years between informant's daughter namely Rinki Kumari (since deceased) and the present petitioner Arjun Mandal and on the pretext of solemnizing marriage, the present petitioner has exploited sexually the deceased.

When the matter came to the knowledge of the informant and other family members, a Panchayati was conveyed and the father of the present petitioner raised a demand of Rs. 5,00,000/- as dowry along with motorcycle and other house hold articles and due to non-fulfillment of the same, the petitioner's marriage was settled with on Rupa Kumari on 09.03.2023.
Thereafter, the deceased instituted a case on 14.03.2023 against the present petitioner for the offence under Section 376 IPC.

sentences.text: The accused persons were threatening to kill the informant and her daughter and on the very next day, killed her daughter.
5. Learned counsel for the petitioner has submitted that the petitioner is innocent and has committed no offence at all as alleged in the FIR rather he has been falsely implicated in this case.

None of the eye- witnesses interrogated during investigation have supported the prosecution story about alleged murder, rather is consistently stated by witnesses that the daughter of the informant had commit suicide on 15.03.2023 at about 1-2 pm and the time of occurrence in the FIR is falsely shown as 4 pm involving all the family members of the petitioner in this fabricated case.
There is no whisper in the entire FIR or the material collected during investigation that the petitioner has played any role in abating the deceased directly or indirectly to commit suicide.
The petitioner is languishing in judicial custody since 18.03.2023 without any rhymes and reasons.
Since charge-sheet has been submitted against the petitioner and he has no criminal background and there is no likelihood of tempering with prosecution evidence and feeling from justice.
Hence the petitioner may be enlarged on bail.

6. On the other hand, learned Addl. P.P. has opposed the prayer for bail of the petitioner and has been submitted that there is direct allegation of serious and heinous offence against the petitioner.
Hence, the petitioner may not be enlarged on bail.

7. From perusal of record, it transpires that as per inquest and postmortem reports of the deceased cause of death has been reserved and viscera has been preserved for chemical examination which has not been received.

It further that during course of investigation, material collected at Paragraphs - 49, 54, 55, 56, 63 of the case diary reveals that due to love affairs between the deceased and the present petitioner, a Panchayati conveyed for the purpose of settlement of marriage which could not succeeded and both parties agreed to solemnize of their daughter and son in their own cost for which a demand of Rs. 5,00,000/- was put by the father of the deceased before the father of the present petitioner but the deceased was adamant to solemnize marriage with the present petitioner.
It also appears that on 15.03.2023 at about 12:50 pm the deceased had committed suicide in her own house.
The version contained in the FIR of the informant as an eye-witness of the occurrence of murder is not found true.
There is no concrete evidence showing any active role of the petitioner in abating the deceased to commit suicide.

8. Considering the facts and circumstances of this case, the nature of allegation against petitioner coupled with materials available on record and period of custody of the petitioner, I am inclined to release the above- named petitioner, on bail.

Accordingly, the petitioner named above, is directed to be released on bail on furnishing bail bond of Rs.25,000/- (Rupees twenty five thousand) with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of learned SDJM, Rajmahal in connection with Rajmahal P.S. Case No. 75 of 2023 with condition that petitioner shall appear physically on each and every date during the trial of case till its conclusion unless his physical appearance is dispensed with for sufficient cause to the satisfaction of the learned trial court and with further condition that petitioner shall not indulge in tampering with the prosecution evidence or influence the witnesses or gain over them.
